title: Regional drip-throttle with weighted circuit states (hotpatch)
author: Noah Chen
release_notes: Hotpatch: introduce regional drip-throttle controller with weighted circuit-state probing and revised defaults to reduce SLO spikes during partial-region overloads. Rollout: canary -> gradual global.
commits: 7f4b2d2: add foundational drip-throttle controller and API hooks
9c3a1ee: integrate weighted circuit state machine and metrics tags
d2b8f7a: adjust defaults, add e2e sim and unit tests, fix flake in probe logic
description:
Motivation: We saw a recurring pattern where partial-region capacity pressure caused abrupt circuit flips and large simultaneous failovers that violated customer latency SLOs. Existing load-shedding is binary per-node and the circuit reset probe is too aggressive, causing oscillation during transient overloads. This hotpatch introduces a "drip-throttle" controller that gracefully sheds traffic in small increments per-region with weighted circuit states to prioritize traffic according to region health and customer tiers.

Design summary: 1) RegionalDripController (traffic-router): periodically computes a small shed fraction for each region based on recent 95th/99th latency and error rate windows; 2) WeightedCircuitState: circuits are no longer binary open/closed—each circuit has a weight (0..1) and a probabilistic probe path that incrementally increases allowed traffic if probes pass; 3) Sticky cooldown and decay: weight increases/decreases use asymmetric time constants to avoid oscillation; 4) Telemetry: new metrics and tags (drip_fraction, circuit_weight, probe_rate, region_priority) and tracing annotations for decision points; 5) Config: degradation policy schema extended with per-region priority and default weights for dedicated vs hosted customers.

What changed (high level files): services/traffic-router/controller/drip_throttle.go - new controller and core algorithm; services/traffic-router/circuit/weighted_state.go - state machine and probe logic; config/schemas/degradation.yaml - new fields for per-region priority and defaults; telemetry/metrics.yaml - new metric definitions and dashboards; tests/e2e/drip_throttle_sim.go - simulation harness used for canary validation; docs/ops/degradation-runbook.md - updated runbook and rollback steps; services/traffic-router/handler/routing_middleware.go - hook to consult controller decision.

Checklist (what I did): [x] unit tests for controller logic and state machine [x] simulation harness with synthetic spike patterns [x] added metrics and dashboards for canary observation [x] instrumentation to tag traces with decisions [x] rollout plan and rollback steps in runbook [x] coordinated canary in us-west-2 for 2 hours then gradual rollout across other regions

Testing and results: Local unit tests and the e2e simulation show substantially lower tail latency and fewer full-circuit flips in scenarios with partial-region CPU pressure. Sim results: under a 30% sustained traffic spike to a subset of hosts, full-circuit count fell by ~78% compared to baseline and 99p latency improved by ~18%. The CI initially failed due to a race in probe cleanup; fixed in commit d2b8f7a and re-run.

Review conversation (abridged): - Maya Patel (review): "Can we avoid adding another periodic goroutine per region? That was causing flakiness in previous controllers." -- Noah: "Implemented a single reconciler tick with per-region state update to avoid goroutine explosion; added a stress test to ensure no drift." - Liam O'Connor (review): "Metrics look good; add an event when circuit_weight crosses 0.8/0.2 boundaries to aid alerting." -- Noah: "Added 'circuit_weight_transition' event and dashboard annotation in telemetry config." - Sofia Ivanov (review): "The default probe cadence seems high for low-tier customers." -- Noah: "Introduced tiered defaults and made them configurable; low-tier defaults have lower probe_rate and longer cooldowns."

CI summary: - Unit tests: initially failed (race in probe cleanup), fixed in second commit and passed. - Linters: minor formatting warnings fixed in commits. - Integration e2e (staging): passed in canary region with synthetic load.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main as hotpatch (squash) 2) Deploy to canary region (us-west-2) behind traffic ramp for 2h while monitoring metrics and SLOs 3) If stable, rollout to mid-tier regions over 24h with automated health checks and auto-rollback on >1% SLO breach 4) Full global rollout after 48h of stable metrics

Rollback: The runbook includes immediate configuration toggle to disable drip controller (degradation.policy.enabled=false) and an automated reversion to prior defaults. Documented manual steps for emergency rollback if needed.

Merge outcome: Approved by Maya Patel and Liam O'Connor after fixes; merged via squash. Post-merge actions: created alert to watch 'drip_fraction' > 0.25 sustained for >15m and a dashboard tile for circuit_weight transitions.

Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative in the control loop to avoid overreaction. Future follow-ups: - take probe success rate into account to accelerate recovery for high-confidence probes - integrate with Dedicated capacity signals to remove shed fraction for reserved nodes - add per-customer override API for escalation during incidents
notes: Canary run completed 2026-02-20 us-west-2. No customer-facing incidents tied to this deploy. Observability tags added to support faster triage.
